C-RELEASE-SIGNING-SPLIT.Summary: Split the release workflow's privileged build job into an unsigned build job and a separate sign job: dependency install scripts and Vite build plugins never again execute in a job that holds signing material, and the only holder of the release-signing environment, the APPLE_*/TAURI_SIGNING_* secrets and the OIDC attestation authority is a sign job that first proves, by SHA-256 digest comparison against the build job's recorded receipts, that what it signs is exactly what the keyless build produced.
C-RELEASE-SIGNING-SPLIT.Problem: Dependencies review finding at commit be2f52f880bc453891ec623169d12b0162b4bd3d, id F-001, key release-build-scripts-share-signing-job, severity high, confidence high, verification result confirmed (the review JSONs number findings differently — the gitleaks finding is F-005 in the dependencies JSON and F-011 in the security JSON; this spec quotes keys, not bare ids). The finding's evidence, quoted verbatim: `what`: "Задание сборки в среде release-signing выполняет npm ci с разрешёнными установочными скриптами. В lock-файле такой скрипт отмечен у esbuild. Позднее Tauri запускает npm run build через beforeBuildCommand в шаге с ключом подписи обновлений и, на macOS, данными подписи Apple. Vite при этом исполняет плагины. На этапе допуска тега уже используется npm ci --ignore-scripts." (EN: the build job in the release-signing environment runs npm ci with install scripts allowed; esbuild is flagged hasInstallScript in the lockfile; Tauri then runs npm run build via beforeBuildCommand in a step holding the updater signing key and, on macOS, Apple signing data; Vite executes plugins there; tag admission already uses npm ci --ignore-scripts.) `impact`: "Скомпрометированная закреплённая зависимость может изменить рабочие файлы до подписи. Установочный шаг предшествует передаче ключей. Сборочные плагины исполняются уже в шаге, которому предоставлены данные подписи. Для запуска требуется допущенный релизный тег." (EN: a compromised pinned dependency can modify working files before signing; the install step precedes key transfer; build plugins execute in the very step that holds signing data; exploitation requires an admitted release tag.) The reviewer's demanded shape (`fix`, EN rendering): install dependencies and build unsigned artifacts in a job without keys, pass verified artifacts to a separate signing job, and allow only necessary install scripts; its verification (`verify`, EN rendering): installation and plugin execution run without signing authority, and the job with keys signs identified input artifacts without rebuilding. Re-verified current topology (release.yml v3.8.0, anchors re-checked 2026-11-22; the notes' v3.7.0-era line numbers shifted): the build job (:383) declares environment: release-signing (:387) with id-token: write and attestations: write (:391-392), runs plain npm ci with lifecycle scripts (:472-473) — esbuild 0.28.2 carries hasInstallScript: true at package-lock.json:6481 — and then the tauri-action steps (:513-526 macOS, :528-535 Windows) carry TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY(_PASSWORD) (:517-518, :532-533) and, on macOS, APPLE_CERTIFICATE(_PASSWORD), APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY, APPLE_ID/PASSWORD/TEAM_ID (:519-524); Tauri's beforeBuildCommand (src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:9) runs npm run build (package.json:11, vite build), executing the Vite plugins (vite.config.js:66-67) inside that same secrets-bearing job; the SLSA provenance and keyless cosign steps that consume id-token: write (:879-889, :900-933) are steps of the same job after packaging. So scripts run before key transfer, build plugins run while signing secrets exist, and OIDC is granted job-wide while only the attestation/signing steps need it — exactly the exposure the finding confirms.
C-RELEASE-SIGNING-SPLIT.Relationship: Resolves the exposure that C-SEC-GITLEAKS-CHECKSUM explicitly deferred as "the separately tracked signing-environment finding"; that change's digest-verification stance (checksum before use, fail closed, red controls on the workflow source) is the pattern reused here for artifact receipts. Stands on the current v3.8.0 boundary and must preserve it: the C-RELEASE-BETA-CHECKS-GATE prerelease checks boundary in authorize-tag and the C-RELEASE-CANARY-PRERELEASE lane stay byte-compatible in behavior, and the stable tag path keeps its admission, publication and cask semantics. Sequencing is normative: the boundary-guard test from the finding notes (§4) lands FIRST as its own leading task in tests/renderer/release-governance.test.js, freezing today's boundary (secrets only in the build job's two tauri steps, id-token: write in no job except build, unsigned lanes secret-free) so any widening while the split lands is detected and consciously reviewed. The target topology has in-repo precedent and is not novel: release-tauri.yml:136-149 already runs an isolated unsigned tauri build without production keys via a config override, and the manual-build job (release.yml:275) is a full unsigned in-workflow builder with contents: read and no environment; only the release lane has not been split. The four authorization-bearing decisions were confirmed by the owner on 2026-11-22 and are restated as this spec's Goals; no open questions remain.

Goals.Goal: Unsigned build job: the release build lane keeps building and packaging both platforms but with no environment, no id-token, no attestations and no secrets.* references anywhere in the job; every signature-dependent step moves out — the APPLE_*/TAURI_SIGNING_* tauri-action invocation, the Developer ID codesign/spctl verification of the signed app (:537-547 today), and the SLSA provenance and cosign steps (:879-933 today). The build job stages UNSIGNED bundles and records a SHA-256 receipt for each staged artifact, reusing the existing *.sha256 sidecar machinery (:721 macOS DMG sidecar, :865-868 Windows installer digest), and uploads them as workflow artifacts (:935-960 today). Gates that work on an unsigned bundle stay in the build job — repeated admission (stable lane), materials, preflight, typecheck, warnings allowlist, attributions, SBOM, updater-fragment composition that does not require a signature, and an unsigned-capable smoke following the release-tauri.yml ad-hoc pattern.

Sign job: a new job, needs-chained on build, carrying environment: release-signing and the id-token: write and attestations: write permissions — the only place they exist in the workflow. It downloads the build job's artifacts, verifies each against the recorded SHA-256 receipts and refuses the run on any mismatch, then performs the Apple import/codesign/notarize/staple flow and the Tauri updater signing for both platform artifact sets; APPLE_* and TAURI_SIGNING_* secrets are referenced only in this job. The SLSA build-provenance and keyless cosign steps move here so provenance and keyless signatures attest the signed release set, and the signed set is uploaded for the downstream publication chain.

Provenance trust model (owner decision 2): the needs-chain (sign runs only after build succeeds in the same workflow run) plus digest comparison against the build job's recorded receipts is the trust model for the handoff — an unsigned artifact whose computed digest does not match its receipt never reaches a signing key. No new attestation format, no node_modules handoff, no cross-run trust; the sign job verifies identified inputs and signs them without rebuilding (the finding's `verify` condition).

Install-script allowlist (owner decision 1): npm ci runs with --ignore-scripts everywhere in the release lane except exactly one approved entry that permits esbuild's install script (the only hasInstallScript package this change allows), matching the tag-admission precedent (authorize-tag already runs npm ci --ignore-scripts at :182). The esbuild entry is conditioned on a dry-run proof that the release build still works under this allowlist; that proof is recorded as an acceptance criterion of this change (live CI evidence), not as a precondition for drafting or approving the spec.

macOS hard lane (owner decision 3): Apple codesigning and notarization happen inside tauri-action's bundling today (build+sign in one step — the tauri-action constraint the notes name), so the split does NOT rebuild in the sign job; the planned approach is to sign the staged unsigned bundle — the sign job re-signs the staged .app, repackages the DMG and updater archive, notarizes and staples — so the signed output is derived from the digest-verified staged bytes rather than from a second build. Which mechanism proves out is recorded with the first live CI run; a silent fallback to rebuild-in-sign is out of bounds (see NonGoals).

Source-pinned structure and docs: tests/renderer/release-governance.test.js gains workflow-structure pins for the split (build job free of environment/id-token/secrets, sign job holding them plus the digest verification step, the needs-chain ordering that keeps publication downstream of signing) with red controls; docs/release-process.md gains a signing section describing the unsigned-build/digest-verified-sign flow and the allowlist; release.yml's own GRACE markup (MODULE_MAP entries for the split jobs, CHANGE_SUMMARY with a version bump), the M-046 SummaryDelta and V-M-046 are synchronized.

Constraints.Constraint: ObservedWriteScope: .github/workflows/release.yml; its source pins in tests/renderer/release-governance.test.js; the new signing section of docs/release-process.md; .grace/graph/features.xml (M-046 SummaryDelta); .grace/verification/features.xml (V-M-046); release.yml's own GRACE markup (MODULE_CONTRACT/MODULE_MAP/CHANGE_SUMMARY with a version bump). No Rust, no renderer product code, no new workflow files, no npm dependency changes, no new secrets, and no change to the release-signing environment's definition or reviewers — only its attachment point moves from build to sign.

The prerelease lane and the beta-checks boundary stay byte-compatible in behavior: authorize-tag is behaviorally untouched (the C-RELEASE-BETA-CHECKS-GATE checks boundary keeps its conditions, pinned set and fail-closed evaluation), prerelease and stable tags flow through the same split build→sign chain, and the prerelease-only skips (admission, materials, preflight, identity artifact) keep their current conditions on whichever job hosts them after the split.

The manual-build and release-tauri.yml precedents are reused as reference topology, not modified: the QA lanes keep their current unsigned, secret-free shape (manual-build permissions contents: read, no environment), and the release-tauri.yml:136-149 isolated dry-run pattern is the cited precedent for unsigned packaging and ad-hoc smoke.

The boundary-guard test lands first as its own task: before any release.yml edit, the governance test suite pins today's boundary (inside the build job only the tauri build steps reference secrets.*, id-token: write exists in no job except build, manual-build and docs-security carry no secrets.*/no environment) so the split's widening is a conscious, reviewed update to a green pin rather than unnoticed drift.

The edit is actionlint-clean; the sign job declares exactly contents/checks/id-token/attestations permissions as needed and no step swallows the digest comparison's exit status; job conditions, concurrency, tag triggers and the publish job's separate release environment with contents: write (publication) keep their current shape.

GRACE bookkeeping is synchronized: release.yml MODULE_MAP gains the split job descriptions, CHANGE_SUMMARY gains the C-RELEASE-SIGNING-SPLIT entry with a version bump, and the graph and verification files describe the new trust boundary. release.yml is the privileged release lane — every edit, including comments, rides the governed process (grace lint current → target → final), and documentation comments are not mixed with secrets, pins or job-condition changes in the same breath.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No changes to tag admission (authorize-tag checks), publication (prepare-publication, the owner-gated publish, feed-advance assertion) or the Homebrew cask handoff (publish-cask); the split stops at the signed artifact set those stages already consume.

No new secrets and no changes to the release-signing environment definition, its reviewers or its tag restriction; no macOS/Windows host behavior claims without CI proof — the repackage/notarize/staple mechanics and the allowlisted-build behavior are proven by actual workflow runs recorded in the change bundle, not asserted from local reasoning.

No allowlist entries beyond esbuild; no reintroduction of lifecycle scripts for platform packages or anything else flagged hasInstallScript; no node_modules or build-cache artifact handoff between jobs (that would recreate the provenance problem this change closes).

No updater-feed schema, latest.json platform shape, WINDOWS_RELEASE staging or counting-gateway URL changes; the feed fragments keep their current composition with signatures produced in the sign job.

No work on the gitleaks download-digest finding (C-SEC-GITLEAKS-CHECKSUM owns it) and no digest or signature pinning for other downloaded tools beyond what this split needs for its own artifact receipts.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Workflow-structure pins (unit): the governance test asserts the build job source contains no environment: declaration, no id-token: or attestations: permission and no secrets.* reference; the sign job source declares environment: release-signing, id-token: write and attestations: write, is the only job referencing APPLE_* or TAURI_SIGNING_* secrets, and contains the digest verification step. Red controls reject a source where the sign job's environment or digest verification is removed, or where secrets.*/id-token reappear in the build job.

Install-shape pins (unit): every npm ci in the release build lane runs with --ignore-scripts, and exactly one allowlisted install-script entry for esbuild exists, commented as the single approved exception; the test rejects a second allowlist entry or a plain npm ci in the build or sign job. The authorize-tag --ignore-scripts precedent (:182) keeps passing.

Provenance pin (unit, workflow-structure test): the sign job's verification step consumes the build job's recorded *.sha256 receipts, recomputes each staged artifact's digest and exits nonzero on mismatch before any signing step; the test pins this ordering (verify-then-sign) with a red control rejecting a sign job that signs before verifying or that swallows the mismatch exit.

Chain pin (unit): sign needs build, and the publication chain (prepare-publication/publish) consumes only the sign job's output set — the needs-chain is pinned so no downstream stage can bypass signing; prepare-publication's current needs list gains the sign dependency explicitly.

CI (live proof): one full prerelease tag (beta or canary) runs green through the split lane — the unsigned build job green with receipts uploaded, the sign job verifying digests and producing the signed, notarized, stapled set with SLSA provenance and keyless cosign, publish exposing the prerelease without advancing releases/latest; the run logs are recorded as the change's live evidence. This same run is the dry-run proof that the esbuild allowlist keeps the release build working under --ignore-scripts elsewhere; a forced digest-mismatch control recorded as refused by the sign job completes the evidence.

GRACE bookkeeping is synchronized and the focused verification is green: release.yml markup updated with a version bump and split-job MODULE_MAP entries, M-046 SummaryDelta present, V-M-046 commands updated, docs/release-process.md signing section in place, actionlint clean on release.yml, and the governance plus action-reference tests pass with the new pins.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedCommand: grace lint --path . --assertions current && grace status --path . --with modules --json
VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Green structural pins with red-control evidence: build job stripped of environment/id-token/secrets, sign job sole holder of signing material and OIDC, verify-then-sign ordering, single esbuild allowlist entry, publication downstream of signing; a workflow diff limited to the split, its GRACE markup and the docs signing section; actionlint clean; after merge, the first beta/canary tag run through the split lane green with the sign job's digest-verification log lines and one forced digest-mismatch refusal recorded in the change bundle.

Assumptions.Assumption: The macOS sign-stage repackage is implementable without a second build: the staged unsigned .app can be re-signed, repackaged into its DMG and updater archive, notarized and stapled by the sign job using standard tooling (codesign, notarytool, stapler, and the tauri signer for updater archives), so tauri-action's build+sign coupling is not a blocker; if a detail proves otherwise, the resolution is an owner-visible decision recorded in the change bundle, not a silent rebuild in the sign job.

The esbuild install script is needed for the release build to work (its postinstall resolves the platform binary); the dry-run/live-tag proof required by the acceptance criteria settles whether the allowlisted entry is strictly necessary and keeps the build green — if the build works without it too, dropping the entry is a permitted tightening, not a scope change.

Workflow artifacts between jobs keep their integrity guarantees (upload/download-artifact within one run is the existing, already-used transport for release-identity and QA handoffs), so needs-chain plus receipt comparison is sufficient provenance for the sign job; a stronger attestation of the unsigned artifacts would be additive hardening, not a requirement of this change.
